card.name: Auxiliary verbs before attributed or related
card.fires_on: Helping verbs such as 'been', 'was' and 'be' (also 'To' and 'We') where the next word is likely 'attributed', 'correlated', 'related' or 'reported'. Seen mostly after 'has' or 'have' in drug-label effect statements.

modes.label: Has/have been before attributed
modes.description: The verb 'been' after 'has' or 'have' in a sentence about an effect, just before a word like attributed or observed.
modes.example: This effect has<< been>> attributed to inhibition of renal prostagland

modes.label: Other helpers before relate or correlate
modes.description: Short helping words in research or label text where a relating or correlating verb could follow.
modes.example: 2)<< To>> relate this information to in-situ data

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words about correlation and relation, such as correlated, relate and correlations.
card.plain: It fires on small helper words like 'been' when the text is about to link one thing to another, as in 'has been attributed to'.
